The Oaks is home to neighbors and staff with roots across these nations and many others, and we're glad to take this month to recognize that shared history.

Property Compliance Notices

Property Masters Inc. (PMI) recently conducted a community walkthrough focused on items stored in public view and fences in need of repair. Some owners received a courtesy notice as a result.

If you received one, please follow the instructions in the letter to resolve the item(s) noted. This walkthrough was not all-inclusive, so additional notices for similar conditions may follow in the days ahead.

Questions or disputes about a notice go through PMI only — not the on-site management office. Log into your owner portal at home.propertymastersinc.net and go to Requests → My Items to respond directly to PMI's support team.

Figures above reflect our financial system as of the date this newsletter was prepared. Community Safety Rounds

Several members of the Oaks Board recently completed a walkthrough of the property with the Houston Police Department, as part of their Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) program. The flyer below covers the resident-facing tips from that walkthrough — additional action items were also identified for management and the Board to address, and a nighttime patrol on October 6 will produce a further report. We'll share updates as each phase wraps up.

New: Interactive Property Map Community Resource

The Oaks now has an interactive property map to help residents, visitors, delivery drivers, and first responders find any unit quickly. It's already installed at the guard house for emergency and delivery use, and it's available to everyone in the community as well — bookmark it, share it, or scan the QR code below.

This map exists because an owner suggested it as an alternative to the posted static map — and we were able to make it happen. It's a good example of how resident feedback turns into real improvements around the property, and it's a living tool that will keep being refined, alongside the new wayfinding signage going up around the property. If you spot an error, have a suggestion for improving it, or have an idea of your own for the community, send it to oaks.director.ljones@gmail.com — we'll incorporate what we can.

Board Meeting Highlights

September 21, 2026 · Downstairs Clubhouse

Attendance

A quorum was present for both the Executive and General sessions. Directors present: Dennis McGregory (President), Steve Jessup (Treasurer), Grace Hively, Kathryn Moose, Catherine Lucas, Sharon Thompson, and Lisa Jones (Secretary). Directors absent: Phyllis Williams and Billy Berry (Vice President). Also present: Jodi Rohrer (PMI/Management) and Shena Powell (Property Manager).

Financial Report (August 2026)

  • The Treasurer reported August income of $387,252.64 against expenses of $224,123.44, a net gain of $163,129.40 for the month.
  • Major expense categories discussed included electricity, gas, water/sewer, and the patrol services contract.
  • The upcoming annual budget is under review by management and the Board before circulation.

Property & Maintenance Updates

  • Tree trimming from the prior work list has been completed; an additional list is planned for October.
  • New reflective building identification signage has been installed throughout the property.
  • Plumbing work for Building 12 was scheduled, with water service notifications planned in advance.
  • A comprehensive roof replacement schedule is being compiled and circulated to the Board for planning purposes.
  • The Board discussed hiring an additional full-time maintenance staff member.
  • Several dumpster enclosure fences have been repainted; additional fencing repairs are planned.
  • A paving contractor is expected to inspect reported potholes and provide pricing.

Landscaping & Irrigation

  • The Board is exploring drought-tolerant and native/adapted landscaping options to reduce water use.
  • Irrigation repairs are ongoing, including troubleshooting a low-irrigation area near the Gessner/fire gate.

Community Safety

  • The Houston Police Department completed a CPTED (Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design) walkthrough of the property. A written report is expected, and recommendations are being reviewed and implemented in phases.
  • A follow-up nighttime assessment of lighting and security conditions is planned.
  • The Board is reviewing security camera options as part of the broader security review; a decision is pending further evaluation.
  • The Board discussed modernizing visitor check-in at the guardhouse.
  • Residents are encouraged to review this issue's CPTED tips for simple steps that help keep the community safe.

Vehicle Accidents / Property Damage

The Board reviewed several recent vehicle accidents involving Association property (poles, carports, fencing). Insurance claims and reimbursement are being pursued where applicable.

Utility Billing

Management continues to reconcile electric account billing following the prior utility service transition, including resolving a billing discrepancy with the provider.

Vantaca / Work Order Communication

The Board is reviewing how work order updates and photos are routed to ensure owners receive clear, timely responses, and that urgent issues (such as active leaks) are prioritized appropriately.

Pest / Animal Remediation

The Board approved a raccoon remediation project for Building 14 (approximately $5,000) and will proactively review prior work orders for animal intrusion issues in other buildings.

Board Election

Preparations for the upcoming Board election are underway, including confirming voting procedures. Details will be communicated to owners as they are finalized.
